prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity north-star desktop web app composition comp, 1536x1024 landscape
Input images: Image 1 is the selected Study Shelf direction reference. Preserve its deep neutral navy field, quiet off-white typography, cobalt focus edge, muted green ready state, restrained academic image tiles, strict rail rhythm, component character, and bilingual density. Do not copy its sidebar, page composition, or exact content thumbnails.
Primary request: Create composition option 3, “Workspace Bridge,” for UniMind’s authenticated bilingual student catalog. The visual world remains The Study Shelf, but the first viewport dramatizes the exact transition from focusing an authorized unit to entering its evidence-aware workspace.
Composition/framing: a slim vertical catalog-path strip occupies about one-fifth of the width and shows validated path stages as compact bilingual labels, not app navigation. The remaining canvas is dominated by one expanded “Cardiovascular Module” shelf tile that bridges browse and workspace: its left half carries the academic subject marker and bilingual identity; its right half exposes Ready status, 12 approved sources, cohort scope, study quota, and a large “Open workspace” action. A horizontal strip of neighboring authorized units runs beneath the dominant tile. A second quiet strip previews Overview, Chat—Coming soon, Studio—Coming soon, and Quiz—Coming soon. Batch Leader and Admin entry points appear only as small role-aware utility links, proving system reach without competing with the student task.
Text: correctly render “Cardiovascular Module”, Arabic “وحدة الجهاز القلبي الوعائي”, “Ready”, Arabic “جاهز”, “Approved sources (12)”, Arabic “المصادر المعتمدة”, “Open workspace”, Arabic “فتح مساحة الدراسة”, “Coming soon”, Arabic “قريبًا”.
Interaction implication: focus expansion is the signature motion; one tile grows while neighbors slide but do not disappear; the action remains a standard button; unavailable units are visibly distinct without revealing private reasons.
Constraints: Operate-mode product UI; serious academic tone; equal desktop/mobile design logic; accessible contrast; long-label tolerance; synthetic data only; no real institution logos; no invented claims; no browser chrome; no device frame; no watermark.
Avoid: entertainment branding, movie posters, autoplay, generic dashboard grids, chatbot-first layout, gamification, glassmorphism, neon glow, gradients, medical organ hero, floating decorative cards, excessive chrome.
